basis: Cerebral small-vessel disease defines the spectrum; damaging ocular, renal and muscle findings vary by subtype without clear umbrella frequencies.
Arrhythmia, phalangeal defects and Pierre-Robin oral abnormalities define the syndrome; impaired smell is reported in 80-99%.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define DEE90; apnea does not establish direct pulmonary damage, and other organ defects are uncommon.
Defined combined immunodeficiency; no additional organ damage is established by the supplied evidence.
Defined hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; TTN association and myopathy ancestry alone do not establish skeletal-muscle involvement.
Chronic neutrophilic folliculitis destroys follicles and causes scarring alopecia; recurrent skin infections are reported in 80-99%.
Pure anxiety disorder; muscle tension, fatigue and concentration symptoms do not establish organ damage.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with progressive visual impairment; optic atrophy remains within the ocular axis.
Venous malformations arise in skin and mucosa, characteristically including lips, tongue and oral mucosa; intestinal bleeding frequency is unspecified.
Retinal degeneration, obesity and polydactyly define BBS21; cognitive impairment is also defining. Renal and dental findings lack frequency support.
Inflammation of tissues around the tooth root, usually driven by infection of a necrotic dental pulp.
Intellectual disability and seizures dominate; conductive hearing impairment occurred in 2/2 assessed patients, supporting ear involvement with limited sampling.
Paraurethral gland neoplasm is classified as a vulvar/reproductive tumor; urinary-tract origin or invasion is not established.
Inherited mitochondrial CoQ10 deficiency; neurologic dysfunction, including ataxia and encephalopathy, affects most. Renal, muscle and cardiac damage varies by subtype.
Supplied phenotype identifies subglottic stenosis and fixed finger contracture/toe anomalies; classic Fraser ocular or renal abnormalities are not established.
Presynaptic neuromuscular-junction disease; fixed contractures and distal arthrogryposis occurred in 1/1 assessed. Respiratory weakness does not establish lung damage.
Degeneration of the macula and posterior retina defines this ocular disease group.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; COL11A1 association alone does not establish skeletal or ocular disease.
Central retinal arterial blockage directly causes retinal ischemia and visual loss; both retinal and arterial disease define the concept.
Congenital cardiac and great-vessel malformations define the syndrome; bronchial compression causing bronchomalacia and respiratory failure is common, approximately >=30%.
Inherited glomerular disease with FSGS in 4/4 and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome in 5/5; no immune mechanism or extrarenal disease established.
Inherited retinal splitting and macular degeneration cause visual loss; associated hemorrhage and detachment remain within the ocular axis.
Esophageal reflux disease; cough alone does not establish airway damage, and aspiration-related pulmonary injury is not common enough to include.
Bile-duct paucity, cardiac defects and ocular abnormalities define it; corneal dystrophy reported in 80-99%. Renal disease occurs in ~40%; vertebral defects omitted at cap.
Defined neurological pain disorder; heterogeneous secondary causes do not justify additional organs across the umbrella.
